articles.title: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and Parallel Queries Walk Into a Bar…
articles.author: Liron Ben Yeda
articles.read_scope: Complete main text and code: request dependency, shared-session TaskGroup, scoped manager, cleanup, and query helper; comments excluded.

practice.trigger: Independent asynchronous database operations fan out within a request.
practice.failure: Tasks share mutable session/transaction state or outlive its resource owner.
practice.mechanism: Give each independent task a context-managed session; retain sequential ownership for one atomic unit.
practice.conditions: Inspect driver, pool budget, isolation, task lifetime, and framework teardown.
practice.limits: Separate sessions do not share atomicity or necessarily a snapshot; parallelism need not improve latency.
practice.counterexample: Sequential request work can safely use one injected session under its transaction contract.
practice.verification: Gate overlapping work, observe independent effects and cleanup, then reuse the bounded pool.

articles.adoption: Adopt ownership problem; use current explicit-session guidance. Do not copy private registry traversal, numeric task-ID scope, or historical timings.
articles.interpretation_limit: No claim that the request-local manager necessarily leaks forever or that every driver produces one shared-session failure mode.

articles.title: Stop the SQLAlchemy Magic: A Guide to Effective Query Testing
articles.author: Liron Ben Yeda
articles.read_scope: Complete main text and code: SQL-file comparison, async query/test snippets, claimed review/debugging benefits; comments excluded.

practice.trigger: ORM query shape obscures a correctness or performance-sensitive database decision.
practice.failure: Approved SQL text conceals wrong parameters/results or an unexecuted async path.
practice.mechanism: Review target-dialect SQL and binds; await execution and assert independently specified results.
practice.conditions: Use representative data and actual result-consumption paths; inspect plans separately for performance.
practice.limits: Compiler snapshots and mocks do not establish database behavior, N+1 absence, or production latency.
practice.counterexample: A simple stable query without a relevant regression risk need not acquire a snapshot test.
practice.verification: Mutate a tenant bind/filter or join and require semantic checks to reject the wrong result.

articles.adoption: Adopt generated-SQL visibility as supplemental review evidence, not the whitespace-stripping comparator or printed unawaited test.
articles.interpretation_limit: Snippet defects are code-inspection findings; the author's unseen production suite was not audited.

crosscheck_access.scope: Only the sections named in each read_scope were read; publication dates were not inferred for undated documentation.

official_crosschecks.title: Session Basics
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Concurrency FAQ, sessionmaker scope, transaction framing, and Closing.
official_crosschecks.finding: Session/AsyncSession are mutable transaction state, used per thread/task; close releases transactional resources but does not necessarily make the object unusable.

official_crosschecks.title: Asynchronous I/O (asyncio)
official_crosschecks.read_scope: ORM synopsis, concurrent tasks, sessionmaker context, scoped-session guidance and close/remove lifecycle.
official_crosschecks.finding: Explicit sessions are preferred for new async designs. Context closure and transaction framing differ. Task-scoped removal belongs in the owning task; closing alone does not remove scope state.

official_crosschecks.title: Contextual/Thread-local Sessions
official_crosschecks.read_scope: ScopedRegistry public interface and scoped-session removal semantics.
official_crosschecks.finding: Public scope operations do not establish private nested-registry enumeration as a lifecycle recipe.

official_crosschecks.title: Built-in Functions: id
official_crosschecks.finding: Object IDs may be reused after an object's lifetime; retaining numeric task keys requires lifecycle care.

official_crosschecks.title: Dependencies with yield; Advanced Dependencies
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Request/function scope, streaming lifetime history, and background-task resources.
official_crosschecks.finding: Current request-scope teardown follows response sending; function scope, added in 0.121.0, precedes it. Background tasks should own resources and receive independent inputs.

official_crosschecks.title: Transaction Isolation
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Read Committed and Repeatable Read visibility and transaction boundaries.
official_crosschecks.finding: Read Committed may see a new snapshot per statement. Repeatable Read stabilizes one transaction, not independently begun transactions.

official_crosschecks.title: SQL Expressions
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Stringification by dialect, binds, literal-rendering limits, and postcompile parameters.
official_crosschecks.finding: Generic rendering is not target-dialect proof; binds are separate. Literal rendering is a limited debugging facility, not secure execution of untrusted values.

official_crosschecks.title: Performance
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Query profiling, cursor execution, result fetching, Cartesian products, and ORM materialization.
official_crosschecks.finding: Locate execution/fetch/materialization cost and inspect backend plans instead of inferring performance from SQL text.

official_crosschecks.title: Relationship Loading Techniques
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Lazy loading/N+1, raiseload, and eager join behavior.
official_crosschecks.finding: Accessing results can emit further queries; a compiled leading statement does not capture the whole loading path.

official_crosschecks.title: unittest.mock: AsyncMock
official_crosschecks.read_scope: AsyncMock call/await distinction, await assertions and await counters.
official_crosschecks.finding: An async mock being called and its result being awaited are separate observations.

official_crosschecks.title: Using EXPLAIN
official_crosschecks.read_scope: Execution-plan interpretation and EXPLAIN ANALYZE execution/side-effect boundary.
official_crosschecks.finding: ANALYZE executes the statement; a plan probe must account for effects and workload representativeness.

version_observations.limit: Documentation versions and requirement pins are not evidence those packages were installed in the inspected interpreter. No dependency installed during this research/reference update.

added: SQLAlchemy task/session versus request dependency boundaries
public scoped cleanup versus historical private manager
awaited semantic query tests and result-consumption observation

runtime_proposals.oracle: Controlled sibling transaction action interferes with shared work; fixed independent tasks preserve each intended transaction, without claiming joint rollback.
Bound pool demand, cancel at controlled acquisition/work boundaries, join cleanup, and execute fresh work through the same pool.
Separate Repeatable Read snapshots may differ; sequential reads in one correctly framed transaction match the declared snapshot contract.
Wrong binds/filter/join produce failing independent result expectations despite plausible SQL text; whitespace normalization and unawaited-call controls expose their limited evidence.

limits: Source/article inspection and package metadata only; no database container, SQLAlchemy/FastAPI runtime, or model evaluation was launched by this update.
Existing framework and transaction choices should change only where the task requires them.
No performance numbers or copyrighted example implementations were copied.
